mg2_starwatcher_1.m: I'm doing adult things. Come back when you're much stronger. Then we can talk.
r: Just you wait, I'll show you.

mg2_starwatcher_10.m: Ten fragments of that burning star scattered along Galmore's bones. They are still warm. Still ... humming.
r: How do you know there are ten pieces?
Ten tongues of light, each flickering in defiance of the dark.
Kealwea, priest of Sullengard, told me so. Now go on.
You can feel that there are ten? Wow.

mg2_starwatcher_14.m: [Ominous voice] In The Ash I Saw Them - Ten Tongues Of Light, Each Flickering In Defiance Of The Dark.

mg2_starwatcher_15.m: Their Number Is Ten. Not Nine. Not Eleven. Ten.

mg2_starwatcher_16.m: So if you have no more questions ...
r: Well, why don't you go and collect them?

mg2_starwatcher_17.m: Only little children could ask such a stupid question. Of course I can't go. Stoutford needs me here.

mg2_starwatcher_18.m: 'Bring these shards to me now. Before the mountain's curse draws worse than beasts to them!
r: In fact I have already found some of these stars.
Enough, please! I can't think when you are talking like this.

mg2_starwatcher_19a.m: So you really don't want to help? And save the world from this disaster?
r: Maybe later. I have to go now.
No, I have enough other things to do.

mg2_starwatcher_19b.m: Woe, woe! Then leave me. I hope you can live with the guilt.

mg2_starwatcher_2.m: You saw it too, didn't you?
r: No, I haven't had any mead today.

mg2_starwatcher_20.m: Kid, I have told you it wasn't a falling star.
r: Anyway, I haven't found any pieces yet.
Anyway, here I have some pieces already.
I might give you half of them - five pieces.
I might give you the rest of them - five pieces.
Anyway, I have found all of the ten pieces.
Anyway, I have found all of the ten pieces, but I have already given them to Kealwea in Sullengard.

mg2_starwatcher_22.m: Don't waste time. Go again and find them. It is urgent!

mg2_starwatcher_24.m: Good, good. But these are not all of them. It must be ten - where are the others?

mg2_starwatcher_25.m: You must be out of your mind! They are deadly - let me destroy all of them.
r: OK, you are right. Here take them and do what you must.
No, I will give you only half of them.

mg2_starwatcher_26.m: Well, I am going to destroy these five. I hope you will be careful with the others and don't rue your decision.
r: I might throw the remaining ones at Andor. Hmm ...

mg2_starwatcher_28.m: Good, good. I'll destroy these dangerous things.
r: Great to hear. And now I have to go and find my brother at last.

mg2_starwatcher_3.m: A tear in the heavens. Not a star falling, but something cast down.

mg2_starwatcher_30.m: Good, good. Give them to me. I'll destroy these dangerous things.
r: I seem to have lost them. Just a minute, I'll look for them ...
But I have already given them to Kealwea in Sullengard.
Here you go. Take it and do what you have to do.
I've changed my mind. These glittery things are too pretty to be destroyed.
Hmm, I still have to think about it. I'll be back...
It was the right thing to do.

mg2_starwatcher_34.m: It is bad. But I won't talk about it anymore.

mg2_starwatcher_4.m: It wept fire. And the mountain answered with a shudder. Such things are not random.

mg2_starwatcher_40.m: You must be out of your mind! Free yourself from them or you are lost!
r: You are certainly right. Take it and do what you have to do.
Now you're exaggerating. I'll go then.

mg2_starwatcher_5.m: He gestured to the dark Galmore montains in the distant south.

mg2_starwatcher_50.m: Wonderful. You have no idea what terrible things this crystal could have done.

mg2_starwatcher_52.m: You did the right thing. The whole world is grateful to you.
r: I do something like that every other day.
I can't buy anything with words of thanks.

mg2_starwatcher_56.m: I have no gold to give...

mg2_starwatcher_60.m: But this necklace with a medal on it will remind you of your heroic deed at any time.

mg2_exploded_star.62: I gave the pieces to Pangitain who was very grateful.
